rationale: Gold is a zero-coupon real asset with no cash flows, so its price should fall as the real risk-free rate rises and the opportunity cost of holding it increases. This is the cleanest theoretical link in the universe and is the pre-specified primary pair.
tradable_note: Gold is traded outright. The real-yield leg would require a TIPS or inflation swap position, which is not in the cash universe, so the hedged variant expresses it as a duration-approximated TIPS position.

rationale: Crude is invoiced in dollars, so a stronger dollar mechanically raises the local-currency cost for non-US buyers and weighs on the dollar price.
tradable_note: The dollar leg is a trade-weighted index, not a directly tradable instrument; replicating it needs an FX basket or dollar-index futures.

rationale: Energy passes into headline inflation, and 10y breakevens historically track the oil complex even though the pass-through to a decade of inflation should be small. Extremes in the residual are candidate over-reactions.
tradable_note: The breakeven leg needs a TIPS-versus-nominal or inflation-swap position. A long breakeven gains when expectations rise, so the residual is scaled by a positive 10y modified duration to express it as a return.

rationale: Implied volatility is a price of insurance on the index, so the two are mechanically linked. The residual measures whether volatility is high or low relative to where the index is trading.
tradable_note: The VIX leg is not investable spot; replicating it requires variance swaps or VIX futures, which carry their own term structure.

rationale: The curve and credit spreads both price the expected path of growth and policy. A curve that is steep relative to credit conditions is a candidate dislocation.
tradable_note: Trading the curve leg requires a duration-weighted 2s10s steepener, whose P&L is not a single-duration transform of the spread. The pair is analysed but cannot be converted into one return series, so it is not backtested.
